name: What is an ADU and how does ADU construction actually work in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: What is an ADU and how does ADU construction actually work in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text:
An ADU is a **self-contained secondary home** on the same lot as your main house, with its own kitchen, bathroom, entrance, and living/sleeping area. In Los Angeles County, ADUs are heavily regulated but strongly supported by state law, so many residential lots qualify.

Most projects follow a predictable path: feasibility review, design, planning approval, building permits, and then construction and inspections. Understanding this sequence helps you avoid costly rework or delays.

Key factors:
- Local zoning (single-family vs multifamily, setbacks, height limits)
- Type of ADU (detached, attached, garage conversion, JADU)
- Utility access (sewer, water, electrical capacity)
- Budget and financing plan

Start by confirming your zoning and basic constraints, then talk with a designer or builder who knows LA County’s ADU rules to shape a realistic plan. Getting the rules clear before you fall in love with a design will save money, time, and stress later.

A team experienced in ADU construction in Los Angeles County can keep you aligned with both state and county requirements from day one.
